subject: math
title: Grade 8 Percents Less Than 1% and Greater Than 100%
seo_title: Grade 8 Percents Less Than 1% and Greater Than 100% Worksheets: Free Math with Answer Key (BC Curriculum)
standard_text: Percents less than 1 and greater than 100 (decimal and fractional percents)
meta_desc: Free Grade 8 math worksheets for the BC curriculum on percents less than 1% and greater than 100%: decimal percents like 0.5%, fractional percents like 12½% and 33⅓%, converting fractions, decimals and percents, and GST and PST, discount and growth problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Change the percent to a decimal, then multiply: 150% = 1.5, 0.5% = 0.005 and 12½% = 0.125.
key_sub: 150% of 60 is 1.5 × 60 = 90, not 60 + 150. 0.5% is half of 1%, not one half, so 0.5% of 4000 is 20. In BC, 5% GST + 7% PST = 12%, so multiply a price by 1.12.
body_html:
Percent means “out of 100”

To use any percent in a calculation, divide it by 100 to get a decimal. Then multiply. This works for 25%, for 150% and for 0.5%.

PercentDecimalFractionSize compared with the whole
150%1.5112more than the whole
100%11the whole
1212%0.12518less than the whole
1%0.011100one hundredth
0.5% = 12%0.0051200half of one hundredth

Percents greater than 100%

100% is the whole amount. A percent greater than 100% gives more than the amount you started with.

Example

What is 150% of 60?

150% = 1.5. 1.5 × 60 = 90.

Answer: 90

Percents less than 1%

A percent less than 1% is a very small part. Find 1% first (divide by 100), then take part of it.

Example

What is 0.5% of 4000?

1% of 4000 = 40. 0.5% is half of 1%: 40 ÷ 2 = 20.

Answer: 20

Fractional percents

A percent can include a fraction, such as 1212% or 3313%. Change the fraction to a decimal (1212% = 12.5%), or use the matching fraction of the whole.

PercentFraction
1212%18
3313%13
3712%38
6623%23
Example

What is 1212% of 64?

1212% = 18. 64 ÷ 8 = 8.

Answer: 8

GST and PST in BC

In BC, most items are charged 5% GST and 7% PST. Together that is 12%, so multiply the price by 1.12.

Sales tax

Headphones cost $60. What is the total with 5% GST and 7% PST?

12% of $60 = 0.12 × 60 = $7.20. $60 + $7.20 = $67.20. Or 1.12 × $60 = $67.20.

Answer: $67.20

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
150% of 60 = 60 + 150 = 210150% = 1.5, so 1.5 × 60 = 90
0.5% = 0.5 (one half)0.5% = 0.5 ÷ 100 = 0.005
0.5% of 4000 = 20001% of 4000 is 40, so 0.5% is 20
1212% of 64 = 12% of 64 = 7.68Keep the half: 1212% = 0.125, so the answer is 8
160% as many as 85 = 85 + 136 = 221“As many” means 160% of 85, so 1.6 × 85 = 136

faq.q: What do Grade 8 students learn about percents in BC?
faq.a: The BC Grade 8 math curriculum includes percents less than 1 and greater than 100, written as decimal percents (0.5%) and fractional percents (12½%). Students use them to solve problems such as sales tax, discounts and population growth.

faq.q: How do you find a percent of a number when the percent is greater than 100%?
faq.a: Write the percent as a decimal and multiply. For 150% of 60, 150% = 1.5 and 1.5 × 60 = 90, which is more than 60 because 150% is more than the whole.

faq.q: How do you find a percent that is less than 1%?
faq.a: Find 1% first by dividing by 100, then take part of it. For 0.5% of 4000, 1% is 40 and 0.5% is half of that, so the answer is 20. Remember that 0.5% is 0.005, not 0.5.

faq.q: How do you calculate GST and PST in BC?
faq.a: BC charges 5% GST and 7% PST on most items, which is 12% in total. Multiply the price by 1.12: a $45 item costs 1.12 × $45 = $50.40 with tax.

sets.title: Percents greater than 100%: 150%, 250% and 450% of a number

items.q: What is 200% of 45?
items.e: 200% = 2, so 200% of 45 = 2 × 45 = 90. 245 adds 200 to 45, 22.5 halves 45 instead of doubling it, and 9 uses 0.2 instead of 2.

items.q: What is 150% of 60?
items.e: 150% = 1.5. 1.5 × 60 = 90. Or: 100% of 60 is 60 and 50% is 30, so 60 + 30 = 90. 210 adds 150 to 60, 30 is only the extra 50%, and 900 uses 15 instead of 1.5.

items.q: What is 300% of 15?
Without calculating, which amount is greater than 90?
items.e: 100% of 90 is 90 itself. A percent greater than 100% gives more than the number, so 110% of 90 is greater than 90. 90% and 99% give less than 90, and 100% gives exactly 90.

items.q: Which calculation finds 175% of 32?
items.e: Percent means out of 100, so 175% = 175 ÷ 100 = 1.75. The calculation is 1.75 × 32 (= 56). 17.5 and 0.175 move the decimal point the wrong number of places, and 32 + 175 adds the percent.

items.q: What is 110% of 70?
What is 125% of 48?
items.e: 125% = 1.25. 100% of 48 is 48 and 25% is 12, so 48 + 12 = 60. 173 adds 125 to 48, 12 is only the extra 25%, and 600 uses 12.5 instead of 1.25.

items.q: What is 120% of 35?
items.e: 120% = 1.2. 100% of 35 is 35 and 20% is 7, so 35 + 7 = 42. 155 adds 120 to 35, 7 is only the extra 20%, and 420 uses 12 instead of 1.2.

items.q: What is 250% of 22?
What is 175% of 36?
What is 105% of 400?
What is 450% of 6?
The double number line shows that 100% is 56. What amount matches 150%?
items.e: On the line, 100% matches 56, so 50% matches 28. 150% = 100% + 50%: 56 + 28 = 84. 206 adds 150 to 56, 28 is only 50%, and 112 is 200%.

items.q: 21 is what percent of 14?
items.e: 2114 = 1.5 = 150%. 21 is more than 14, so the answer must be more than 100%. 50% is only the extra 7, 1.5% forgets to multiply by 100, and 7% uses the difference.

items.q: 52 is what percent of 16?
items.e: 5216 = 3.25 = 325%. Check: 3.25 × 16 = 52. 225% is only the extra 36 compared with 16, 3.25% forgets to multiply by 100, and 36% uses the difference 52 − 16.

items.q: Which statement is true?
Which is greater: 250% of 12 or 12% of 250?
items.e: 250% of 12 = 2.5 × 12 = 30. 12% of 250 = 0.12 × 250 = 30. They are equal: a% of b is always the same as b% of a.

items.q: What percent of 80 is 200?
items.e: 20080 = 2.5 = 250%. 200 is more than 80, so the percent is more than 100%. 120% uses the difference 200 − 80, 40% divides the wrong way (80 ÷ 200), and 2.5% forgets to multiply by 100.

items.q: 125% of a number is 50. What is the number?
items.e: 1.25 × ? = 50, so ? = 50 ÷ 1.25 = 40. Check: 125% of 40 = 40 + 10 = 50. 62.5 is 125% of 50 (the wrong way round), 37.5 takes 25% of 50 away, and 400 divides by 0.125.

items.q: 300% of a number is 84. What is the number?
items.e: 300% = 3, so 3 × ? = 84 and ? = 84 ÷ 3 = 28. 252 is 300% of 84 (the wrong way round), 280 divides by 0.3, and 0.28 divides by 300 without changing the percent to a decimal.

sets.title: Percents less than 1%: 0.5%, 0.25% and 0.1% of a number

items.q: What is 1% of 3000?
What is 0.5% of 4000?
What is 0.1% of 6000?
What is 0.5% of 600?
items.e: 1% of 600 is 6, so 0.5% is half of 6 = 3. 300 treats 0.5% as one half, 30 is 5%, and 0.3 is 0.05%.

items.q: The grid has 100 equal squares. What percent of the grid is shaded?
items.e: One whole square is 1% of the grid. Only half of one square is shaded, so the shaded part is 0.5%: less than 1%. 50% would be half of the whole grid.

items.q: What is 0.25% of 800?
What is 0.2% of 2500?
What is 0.1% of 35 000?
What is 0.6% of 1500?
What is 0.3% of 7000?
4 is what percent of 1000?
items.e: 41000 = 0.004. Multiply by 100: 0.4%. 4% would be 40 out of 1000.

items.q: 1 is what percent of 200?
items.e: 1200 = 0.005 = 0.5%. Check: 1% of 200 is 2, so 1 is half of 1%. 50% mixes up 1200 with 12, 5% moves the decimal point 3 places, and 0.005% forgets to multiply by 100.

items.q: What is 0.8% of 250?
What is 0.05% of 40 000?
What is 0.75% of 2400?
What is 0.5% of 48?
items.e: 1% of 48 is 0.48. 0.5% is half of that: 0.24. 24 treats 0.5% as one half, 2.4 is 5%, and 0.024 is 0.05%.

items.q: Which amount is less than 1% of 600?
items.e: 1% of 600 = 6. 0.9% of 600 = 5.4, which is less, so 0.9% of 600. 1.1% of 600 = 6.6, and 10% of 60 and 2% of 300 are both exactly 6.

items.q: Which list is in order from least to greatest?
items.e: Compare the decimals: 0.07 < 0.60 < 1. So 0.07%, 0.6%, 1%. 0.07% has the digit 7, but it is less than one tenth of 1%.

items.q: Which is equal to 0.5% of 600?
0.5% of a number is 9. What is the number?
items.e: 0.5% = 0.005, so ? = 9 ÷ 0.005 = 1800. Or: 0.5% is 9, so 1% is 18 and 100% is 1800. 18 divides by 0.5 (treats 0.5% as 0.5), 4.5 takes half of 9, and 180 divides by 0.05.

sets.title: Fractional percents: 12½%, 33⅓% and ½% of a number

items.q: Write 1212% as a decimal.
items.e: 1212% = 12.5%. Divide by 100: move the decimal point 2 places left. 12.5% = 0.125. 0.12 drops the half, 1.25 moves only one place, and 12.5 forgets to divide.

items.q: Write 1212% as a fraction in simplest form.
items.e: 1212% = 12.5100 = 1251000 = 18. 325 is 12% (the half is dropped), 180 is 1.25%, and 252 is 1212 itself, not divided by 100.

items.q: Write 14% as a decimal.
items.e: 14% = 0.25%. Divide by 100: 0.0025. 0.25 forgets to divide (that is 25%), 0.025 moves only one place, and 25 multiplies by 100 instead of dividing.

items.q: Write 18 as a percent.
items.e: 1 ÷ 8 = 0.125. Multiply by 100: 12.5% = 1212%. 8% uses the denominator, 18% joins the digits, and 18% forgets to multiply by 100.

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 3313%?
items.e: 3313% means 3313 out of 100. Since 3 × 3313 = 100, this is 13. 33100 drops the 13, 133 uses 33 as the denominator, and 310 is 30%.

items.q: Write 1200 as a percent.
items.e: 1 ÷ 200 = 0.005. Multiply by 100: 12% (0.5%). 50% mixes up 1200 with 12, 200% uses the denominator, and 0.005% forgets to multiply by 100.

items.q: The grid has 100 equal squares. What percent of the grid is shaded?
items.e: 12 whole squares are shaded (12%) and then half of one more square (12%). 12% + 12% = 1212%. 25% doubles the count, 12% leaves out the half square, and 13% counts the half square as a whole one.

items.q: What is 12% of 1200?
items.e: 12% means half of 1%, not half. 1% of 1200 is 12, so 12% is 6. 600 treats 12% as one half (50%), 60 is 5%, and 0.6 is 0.05%.

items.q: What is 212% of 400?
items.e: 1% of 400 is 4. 212% = 2.5 × 4 = 10. 8 is only 2% (the half is dropped), 100 is 25%, and 1 is 0.25%.

items.q: What is 14% of 2000?
items.e: 1% of 2000 is 20. 14% is a quarter of 1%: 20 ÷ 4 = 5. 500 is 25%, 50 is 2.5%, and 0.5 is 0.025%.

items.q: What is 1212% of 64?
items.e: 1212% = 18, so 1212% of 64 = 64 ÷ 8 = 8. 7.68 is only 12% (the half is dropped), 80 uses 1.25, and 0.8 uses 0.0125.

items.q: What is 112% of 600?
items.e: 1% of 600 is 6, and 12% of 600 is 3. 112%: 6 + 3 = 9. 6 is only 1% (the half is dropped), 90 is 15%, and 0.9 is 0.15%.

items.q: What is 3313% of 27?
items.e: 3313% = 13, so 3313% of 27 = 27 ÷ 3 = 9. 8.91 uses 0.33 × 27, which is a little too small, 81 multiplies by 3, and 0.9 is 313%.

items.q: What is 614% of 160?
items.e: 614% = 6.25% = 116, so 160 ÷ 16 = 10. 9.6 is only 6% (the quarter is dropped), 100 uses 0.625, and 1 uses 0.00625.

items.q: What is 3712% of 48?
items.e: 3712% = 38. 48 ÷ 8 = 6, and 3 × 6 = 18. 30 is 58 of 48, 17.76 is only 37% (the half is dropped), and 180 uses 3.75.

items.q: What is 6623% of 45?
items.e: 6623% = 23. 45 ÷ 3 = 15, and 2 × 15 = 30. 15 is only 13, 29.7 uses 0.66 × 45, and 300 uses 623 instead of 23.

items.q: What is 8712% of 40?
items.e: 8712% = 78. 40 ÷ 8 = 5, and 7 × 5 = 35. 5 is only 1212% (the part left out), 34.8 is only 87%, and 350 uses 8.75.

items.q: Write 58 as a percent.
items.e: 5 ÷ 8 = 0.625. Multiply by 100: 62.5% = 6212%. 58% joins the digits, 614% multiplies by 10 instead of 100, and 160% is 85 (the fraction flipped).

items.q: Which is equal to 1212% of 80?
items.e: 1212% of 80 = 80 ÷ 8 = 10. 25% of 40 = 40 ÷ 4 = 10 too, so 25% of 40. 12% of 80 = 9.6, 1212% of 8 = 1, and 25% of 80 = 20.

items.q: 1212% of a number is 9. What is the number?
items.e: 1212% = 18, so 9 is one eighth of the number: 9 × 8 = 72. Check: 72 ÷ 8 = 9. 112.5 multiplies 9 by 12.5, 0.72 divides 9 by 12.5, and 1.125 is 1212% of 9 (the wrong way round).

items.q: Write 0.5% as a decimal.
items.e: Percent means out of 100, so divide by 100: move the decimal point 2 places left. 0.5% = 0.005. 0.5 forgets to divide (0.5 is 50%), 0.05 moves only one place, and 5 multiplies by 10.

items.q: Write 175% as a decimal.
items.e: Divide by 100: 175% = 175 ÷ 100 = 1.75. 175% is more than 100%, so the decimal is more than 1.

items.q: Write 0.09 as a percent.
items.e: Multiply by 100: move the decimal point 2 places right. 0.09 = 9%. 90% would be 0.9.

items.q: Write 3.2 as a percent.
items.e: Multiply by 100: 3.2 × 100 = 320%. 3.2 is more than 1, so the percent is more than 100%. 32% moves the decimal point only one place.

items.q: Write 0.006 as a percent.
items.e: Multiply by 100: 0.006 × 100 = 0.6%. The number is less than 0.01, so the percent is less than 1%.

items.q: Write 0.45% as a decimal.
items.e: Divide by 100: move the decimal point 2 places left. 0.45% = 0.0045. 0.45 forgets to divide, and 0.045 moves only one place.

items.q: Write 1.08 as a percent.
items.e: 1.08 × 100 = 108%. 10.8% moves the decimal point only one place, and 18% drops the zero.

items.q: Write 78 as a percent.
items.e: 7 ÷ 8 = 0.875. Multiply by 100: 87.5%. 7.8% reads 78 as 7.8, 0.875% forgets to multiply by 100, and 12.5% is 18.

items.q: Write 74 as a percent.
items.e: 7 ÷ 4 = 1.75 = 175%. The fraction is more than 1, so the percent is more than 100%. 1.75% forgets to multiply by 100, and 74% joins the digits.

items.q: Write 1250 as a percent.
items.e: 1 ÷ 250 = 0.004. Multiply by 100: 0.4%. 4% would be 125, 250% uses the denominator, and 0.004% forgets to multiply by 100.

items.q: Which is equal to 1500?
items.e: 1500 = 0.002. Multiply by 100: 0.2%. 2% is 150.

items.q: Which is equal to 0.8%?
items.e: 0.8% = 0.8 ÷ 100 = 0.008 = 81000 = 1125. 0.08 is 8%, 0.8 is 80%, and 8 is 800%.

items.q: Write 0.3% as a fraction.
items.e: 0.3% = 0.3100. Multiply top and bottom by 10: 31000. 310 is 30%, and 3100 is 3%.

items.q: Write 225% as a mixed number.
items.e: 225% = 225100 = 2.25 = 214. 2212 divides by 10 instead of 100, 225 reads .25 as “2 over 5”, and 14 forgets the 2 wholes.

items.q: Write 135 as a percent.
items.e: 135 = 1.6. Multiply by 100: 160%. 60% forgets the whole, and 1.6% forgets to multiply by 100.

items.q: Which is greater: 0.6% or 0.06?
items.e: Write both as decimals. 0.6% = 0.006. 0.06 > 0.006, so 0.06 is greater (0.06 = 6%).

items.q: Which number is greatest?
items.e: Write all as decimals: 1.4, 135% = 1.35, 118 = 1.375, 0.9% = 0.009. The greatest is 1.4. 135 looks big, but 135% is only 1.35.

items.q: Which is not equal to 2.5?
items.e: 250% = 2.5, 52 = 2.5 and 212 = 2.5. 25% = 0.25, so it is not equal to 2.5.

items.q: Which list is in order from least to greatest?
items.e: Write all as decimals: 99% = 0.99, 1.05, 118 = 1.125. So the order is 99%, 1.05, 118. 99% is just under 1.

items.q: Which shows 3400 as a decimal and as a percent?
items.e: 3 ÷ 400 = 0.0075. Multiply by 100: 0.75%. So 0.0075 and 0.75%. 0.0075% forgets to multiply by 100, and the others put the decimal point in the wrong place.

sets.title: Word problems: GST and PST, discounts and growth

items.q: Noah buys headphones for $60. BC charges 5% GST and 7% PST. What is the total with tax?
A snowboard costs $250. How much PST (7%) is charged on it?
Owen has $2400 in a savings account that pays 0.5% interest a month. How much interest does he earn in one month?
items.e: 1% of $2400 = $24, so 0.5% is half of that: $12. $1200 treats 0.5% as one half, $120 is 5%, and $1.20 is 0.05%.

items.q: Last year, 85 students ran in their school’s Terry Fox Run. This year, 160% as many students ran. How many students ran this year?
items.e: “160% as many” means 160% of 85: 1.6 × 85 = 136. 245 adds 160 to 85, 221 increases 85 by 160%, and 51 is only the extra 60%.

items.q: A board game costs $45. BC charges 5% GST and 7% PST. What is the total with tax?
items.e: 12% of $45 = $5.40, so the total is $45 + $5.40 = $50.40. Or 1.12 × $45 = $50.40. $57 adds 12 dollars, $47.25 adds only the GST, and $48.15 adds only the PST.

items.q: A hockey stick costs $96. A Kamloops sports store takes 1212% off. What is the sale price?
items.e: 1212% = 18, so the discount is $96 ÷ 8 = $12. $96 − $12 = $84. $12 is only the discount, $83.50 takes 12.5 dollars off, and $108 adds the discount.

items.q: Ryan’s phone plan includes 8 GB of data a month. This month he used 10 GB. What percent of his plan did he use?
items.e: 108 = 1.25 = 125%. Ryan used more than the plan, so the answer is more than 100%. 25% is only the extra, 1.25% forgets to multiply by 100, and 80% divides the wrong way.

items.q: A town in the Okanagan has 15 000 people. The population grows by 4%. What is the new population?
items.e: 4% of 15 000 = 600. 15 000 + 600 = 15 600. 15 004 adds 4 people, 600 is only the growth, and 21 000 grows by 40%.

items.q: Last year, 4000 salmon returned to a creek on Vancouver Island. This year, 250% as many returned. How many salmon returned this year?
A Burnaby factory makes 25 000 light bulbs in a week. 0.4% of them are faulty. How many bulbs are faulty?
In November, 200 mm of rain fell in Vancouver. In December, 170 mm fell. What is the percent decrease?
items.e: Decrease = 200 − 170 = 30 mm. Divide by the starting amount: 30200 = 0.15 = 15%. 30% uses the 30 mm as a percent, 85% is December as a percent of November, and 1.5% moves the decimal point only one place.

items.q: The number of daily riders at a SkyTrain station grew from 20 000 to 25 000. What is the percent increase?
items.e: Increase = 5000. Divide by the starting number: 500020 000 = 0.25 = 25%. 20% divides by the new number (500025 000), 125% is the new number as a percent of the old one, and 2.5% multiplies by 10 instead of 100.

items.q: In ski season, a Whistler hotel charges 140% of its usual price. The usual price is $200 a night. What is the ski-season price?
items.e: 140% of $200 = 1.4 × 200 = $280. $340 adds 140 dollars, $80 is only the extra 40%, and $480 increases $200 by 140%.

items.q: A condo in Vancouver is worth $650 000. Its value rises by 0.5%. By how much does the value rise?
Harjot buys a $35 lacrosse stick. BC charges 5% GST and 7% PST. How much more is the PST than the GST?
items.e: PST: 7% of $35 = $2.45. GST: 5% of $35 = $1.75. $2.45 − $1.75 = 70¢ (that is 2% of $35). $2 subtracts the rates as dollars, $4.20 is both taxes together, and $1.75 is only the GST.

items.q: At an eagle count near Squamish, volunteers counted 1200 bald eagles one year. The next year the count was 3313% higher. How many eagles were counted the next year?
items.e: 3313% = 13. 1200 ÷ 3 = 400, so the count is 1200 + 400 = 1600. 400 is only the increase, 1596 uses 33% instead of 3313%, and 800 is a decrease.

items.q: A town of 20 000 people grows by 5% each year for 2 years. What is the population after 2 years?
items.e: After 1 year: 5% of 20 000 = 1000, so 21 000. After 2 years: 5% of 21 000 = 1050, so 21 000 + 1050 = 22 050. 22 000 adds 5% of 20 000 twice, but the second 5% is of the bigger number. 21 000 is only one year, and 20 010 adds just 5 people a year.

items.q: Snowboard boots cost $120. They are 25% off, and then 5% GST and 7% PST are added to the sale price. What is the total?
items.e: 25% of $120 = $30, so the sale price is $90. 12% of $90 = $10.80. $90 + $10.80 = $100.80. $134.40 forgets the discount, $90 forgets the tax, and $104.40 takes off 25% − 12% = 13%.

items.q: A hiking club grew by 1212% and now has 72 members. How many members did it have before?
items.e: After the growth the club has 112.5% of the old number. 1212% = 18, so the old number plus one eighth of it is 72: 98 × ? = 72, and ? = 72 ÷ 9 × 8 = 64. Check: 64 ÷ 8 = 8, and 64 + 8 = 72. 63 takes 1212% of 72 away, but the 1212% is of the old number. 81 adds it on, and 60 takes away 12.

items.q: Ski goggles cost $84 including 5% GST and 7% PST. What was the price before tax?
items.e: The total is 112% of the price: 1.12 × ? = $84, so ? = $84 ÷ 1.12 = $75. Check: 12% of $75 = $9, and $75 + $9 = $84. $73.92 takes 12% of $84 away, but the tax is 12% of the price before tax. $72 takes away 12 dollars, and $9 is only the tax.
